root_cause.text: The `check_rkey()` function in `drivers/infiniband/sw/rxe/rxe_resp.c` lacked a strict length check for ATOMIC_WRITE requests, allowing zero-length packets (where `pktlen` == `resid` == 0) to bypass validation because the existing logic only compared `pktlen` against `resid`, so a remote initiator could reach `atomic_write_reply()` which unconditionally reads 8 bytes from `payload_addr(pkt)`, causing an out-of-bounds read of skb tailroom memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a new length check specifically for `RXE_ATOMIC_WRITE_MASK` requiring `resid == sizeof(u64)`, `pktlen == sizeof(u64)`, and `bth_pad(pkt) == 0`, and the commit message states: "check_rkey() previously accepted an ATOMIC_WRITE request with pktlen == resid == 0 because the length validation only compared pktlen against resid."

intent_record.what: Split the combined condition for RXE_WRITE_MASK and RXE_ATOMIC_WRITE_MASK into two separate branches. For atomic writes (RXE_ATOMIC_WRITE_MASK), added a new length check requiring resid == sizeof(u64), pktlen == sizeof(u64), and bth_pad(pkt) == 0, otherwise set error state RESPST_ERR_LENGTH. For writes (RXE_WRITE_MASK), the existing logic (resid > mtu then check pktlen == mtu and no pad) remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, atomic write packets are now validated to have exactly 8 bytes of payload and no BTH pad. Previously, they shared the write path which only checked if resid > mtu, allowing invalid lengths. This prevents reading beyond the packet buffer and enforces the IB specification.
